item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 221725
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on recently
downgraded Tropical Depression Fay, located several hundred miles
southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
A tropical wave is forecast to move off the coast of western Africa
tomorrow. Although upper-level winds are not very conducive, some
slow development of this system is possible while it moves generally
northwestward across the far eastern Atlantic. Interests in the
Cabo Verde Islands should monitor the progress of this system as
gusty winds and areas of heavy rain are possible there by the end of
the week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay Public Advisory Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 222036
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay Advisory Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026
 
...FAY DEGENERATES TO A REMNANT LOW PRESSURE AREA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...30.8N 35.3W
ABOUT 685 MI...1105 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 240 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1011 MB...29.86 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay 
was located near latitude 30.8 North, longitude 35.3 West. The 
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the west-southwest near 9 mph 
(15 km/h). A gradual turn toward the west is expected during the 
next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts. 
The remnant low is expected to gradually weaken during the next few 
days.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1011 mb (29.86 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane
Center on this system. Additional information on this system can be 
found in High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather 
Service, under AWIPS header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and 
online at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay Forecast Discussion Number 14
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 222037
TCDAT1
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Fay Discussion Number  14
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Tue Sep 22 2026

Fay remains mainly comprised of a swirl of low- to mid-level clouds, 
although a few isolated patches of convection are occuring in the 
eastern semicircle. There has been no organized convection for more 
than 18 h, and based on this it appears than Fay has degenerated to 
a remnant low pressure area. There is a possibility of convective 
bursts occuring during the next few days. However, the cyclone will 
be embedded in a dry air mass with strong upper-level convergence, 
and these factors should keep organized convection from 
re-developing.
 
The system is moving west-southwestward, or 240/8 kt, as it rounds 
the eastern periphery of a low- to mid-level ridge to its west and 
northwest. A turn toward the west is expected over the next day or 
two as the ridge strengthens and builds eastward to the north of 
Fay. A turn toward the west-northwest could occur before the remnant 
low dissipates between 96-120 h.

This is the last advisory issued on Fay by the National Hurricane 
Center. Additional information on this system can be found in High 
Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service, under AWIPS 
header NFDHSFAT1, WMO header FZNT01 KWBC, and online at 
ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFAT1.php
